light: This is one ordinary frame pulled from a normal handheld home video shot by his grandson with a consumer camera at eye level, simply recording what happens, not composing a photo. The framing is casual and a little off: something is cut by the edge of the frame. Almost everything in the frame is in focus, nothing blurred out: the cluttered cabin background stays fully readable. The only light is what the place really has, and each person and object gets light according to where it stands; correctly exposed and bright enough, the side near the snowy window brighter and cooler, the corners by the stove a little warmer. Colours of an ordinary video with automatic white balance and almost no correction: moderate contrast, soft highlights, mild sensor noise and light compression, faint motion blur on anything moving. Skin with pores, age spots and uneven tone; white hair and beard with stray hairs; flannel and canvas apron with real creases, soot and grease marks. People are caught mid-action, unposed. Bright snowy daylight from the window on the left plus the warm glow of the wood stove.
look: Ordinary handheld home video filmed by his grandson with a consumer camera at eye level, small natural shakes and casual slightly imperfect framing, everything in the cabin in focus, only the light the place really has, bright and correctly exposed, automatic white balance, mild sensor noise; real skin and natural old hands; he moves naturally and unposed, nothing staged; no music.

anchors.prompt: Same cabin, same moment of the day. Ole, a 78-year-old man with thinning white hair, a short full white beard, a dark green and black plaid flannel shirt over a cream henley undershirt and a worn tan canvas apron, big old hands with age spots and veins stands next to the black cast iron wood cookstove with its stovepipe going up through the ceiling and a small firebox door with a glowing orange fire behind the mica window in the log cabin cook shack of an old north-woods logging camp: weathered log walls, a black cast iron wood cookstove with a stovepipe and a small glowing firebox door, a window with snow outside, a two-man crosscut saw and an axe hanging on the log wall, bunk beds with plaid wool blankets at the left, a rough plank table with a blue enamel mug. One hand rests on the firebox door handle and the other hand is open, waving the viewer in toward the room, he looks at the camera and talks, mouth mid-word. Medium shot from about one and a half meters, the stove and its pipe at the right of the frame, the snowy window at the left, the plank table at the bottom edge.
A second later, same place: he jerks his thumb back over his shoulder at the cabin door behind him, then looks at the camera again with a small welcoming smile, mouth mid-word.
Same place, a few seconds later: he pats the flat iron top of the stove with his open palm like it is an old friend, a dry little grin under the white beard, eyebrows raised, looking at the camera.

clips.text: Well, now, friend, come on in and shut that door behind you.
clips.action: He waves the viewer in with his open hand and then jerks a thumb back at the cabin door, welcoming. He wears the same dark green and black plaid flannel shirt, cream henley and tan canvas apron the whole time.

clips.text: The stove's the only thing in this camp kitchen that never asks for a raise.
clips.action: He pats the iron stove top with his palm and leans toward the camera with a sly grin. He wears the same dark green and black plaid flannel shirt, cream henley and tan canvas apron the whole time.

clips.text: And I'm going to show you the trick. It's not magic,
clips.action: He holds up one finger, serious, then opens both hands in an honest shrug. He wears the same dark green and black plaid flannel shirt, cream henley and tan canvas apron the whole time.

clips.text: And one little handle on the pipe that people either never touch or turn the wrong way.
clips.action: He points up along the stovepipe and then shakes his head slowly at the camera. He wears the same dark green and black plaid flannel shirt, cream henley and tan canvas apron the whole time.

clips.text: But before I strike a single match, four things,
clips.action: He holds up a wooden match between two fingers and then puts the box of matches on the shelf. He wears the same dark green and black plaid flannel shirt, cream henley and tan canvas apron the whole time.

clips.text: Because a stove is a good friend only when you treat it right.
clips.action: He pats the side of the stove fondly and then nods at the camera, kind and serious. He wears the same dark green and black plaid flannel shirt, cream henley and tan canvas apron the whole time.

clips.text: You can't see that gas or smell it, and it gives you a headache and dizziness and you never figure out why.
clips.action: He explains with an open hand, then taps two fingers to his temple with a squint. He wears the same dark green and black plaid flannel shirt, cream henley and tan canvas apron the whole time.

clips.text: Quick word, friend, while I've got you. Everything I cook on this stove, I've been writing down:
clips.action: He talks to the camera while he writes in the notebook, then lifts the notebook toward the camera with a proud smile. He wears the same dark green and black plaid flannel shirt, cream henley and tan canvas apron the whole time.

clips.text: Here is the mistake I made when I was young. I closed it right down to make the wood last all night.
clips.action: He shakes his head ruefully with a hand on the damper handle, then lets go and raises a finger with a wry smile. He wears the same dark green and black plaid flannel shirt, cream henley and tan canvas apron the whole time.

clips.text: Tell me in the comments: what do you burn in your stove, and how do you know it's dry? I read every one. Now put another split on. Not too many, mind you. And I'll see you in the next one.
clips.action: He talks to the camera from the table, then raises the mug with a kind smile and a goodbye nod. He wears the same dark green and black plaid flannel shirt, cream henley and tan canvas apron the whole time.
